_comment: Log read for /observability > Logs. Attach to IAM user
mcaffeine-erp-prefg-tool in account 157320387454 — the identity behind
ACCESS_KEY_ID_AWS / SECRET_ACCESS_KEY_AWS in SSM /erp-app/*.
Suggested policy name: erp-app-observability-logs
WHY ITS OWN POLICY, not another statement in iam-policy-erp-app-deploy.json:
same reasoning that file's SES sibling gives — one concern per policy stays
independently reviewable and can be detached without touching the deploy
path that ECR, SSM and EC2 depend on.
WHY SCOPED, when every statement in the deploy policy uses '*':
these keys already carry ssm:SendCommand with AWS-RunShellScript on both app
instances plus read/write on all /erp-app/* secrets (see the SECURITY NOTE in
iam-policy-erp-app-runtime-ses.json). Application logs are the app's own
output and carry user names, email addresses, PO numbers and request paths,
so the marginal grant is held to the two groups the CloudWatch agent writes:
/erp/app and /erp/bootstrap (deploy/cloudwatch-agent-config.json).
Do NOT widen Resource to '*' to reach an unrelated log group — add a second
statement naming that group instead.
BOTH ARNs are required. FilterLogEvents authorises against the log-group ARN,
but the ':log-stream:*' form is what several logs actions check, and omitting
it produces an AccessDenied that names the group and so reads as if the group
ARN were wrong. Listing both widens nothing.
Logs Insights (logs:StartQuery, logs:GetQueryResults, logs:StopQuery) is
deliberately NOT granted. lib/aws/cloudwatch.ts uses the synchronous
FilterLogEvents, and aggregation over logs is already done in SQL on the
Requests tab — faster, and joined to users, which Insights cannot do.
This grants READ only. Nothing in the app writes to CloudWatch Logs; the
agent on the instance does that under the instance role, not these keys.

_comment_describe: DescribeLogGroups does not support resource-level permissions — it is a
list operation over the account, so '*' is the only expressible form.
It is already granted by the deploy policy; listed here so this policy
works standalone if that one is ever detached.
